summary.tldr: Lets some parents and grandparents visiting Canada use approved foreign health insurance, stay up to five years, and adds reporting on income rules.
what_it_does: Allows a parent or grandparent applying for a visitor visa for an extended stay to use a health insurance policy bought from an approved insurer outside Canada.
Sets the allowed stay for a temporary resident visiting a Canadian citizen or permanent resident child or grandchild at five years.
Requires the Minister of Citizenship and Immigration to report on lowering the minimum income requirement a child or grandchild must meet for an extended visit.
Requires the report to cover special circumstances in visa processing and a review process for those decisions, and to be tabled in Parliament and published online.
Requires the minister to table a statement of reasons if no income change or related process is provided within two years after royal assent.
who_it_affects: Canadian citizen and permanent resident families
Foreign nationals applying for extended visits
Foreign insurers approved by the minister
summary.background: The bill amends the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act. It deals with temporary resident visas for parents and grandparents visiting Canadian citizen or permanent resident children or grandchildren.
